answer: A market for prism calibration in ridge-to-inlet surveys admits agents through human sponsors. An issuer deduplicates people and gives each one credential bound to a fixed secret. A sponsor proves possession in zero knowledge and publishes H(secret, epoch). Validators check the proof and reject a second use of that nullifier, regardless of agent key. Parallel aliases need separately enrolled people, paying each sponsor's recruitment cost. Proofs cannot be replayed across epochs. This assumes honest deduplication and scarce willing sponsors; paid collusion remains possible.
